Three lines of work run through this site. Each connects the posts here to
published research, talks, and software in development.

The through-line has been **representation** — how experience changes the
discriminability of similar things, and what follows for how we measure them.

---

<p class="section-label">◉ Representation and Measurement</p>

The early work was experimental: how associative learning and perceptual
experience alter the discriminability of similar stimuli, and what general
processes of representation that implies.

The same question now arises in psychological measurement. Psychology has
accumulated thousands of constructs, many of which may be alternative
descriptions of the same conceptual territory. Determining which are genuinely
distinct has historically required new data. Advances in language modelling
suggest the linguistic content from which constructs are built may already
carry much of the necessary structure.

Current work asks whether the geometry of language can differentiate profiles
that scalar construct scores collapse — and what that implies for what
measurement is delivering in the first place.

*In progress:* Bloom's taxonomy verbs in embedding space (London Text Analysis
Conference, 2026); semantic maps of self-concept (in preparation).

<p class="section-label">◉ Cognitive Extension and System Design</p>

Recent AI capabilities have been characterised as *System 0* — a layer of the
cognitive stack that performs inference, shaping information before it reaches
intuitive or analytical thought. This raises design questions rather than
merely philosophical ones: how tightly should such systems integrate, along
what dimensions, and what makes the resulting cognitive ergonomics good or bad.

<p class="section-label">◉ Evaluation and Institutions</p>

Measurement frameworks are not neutral instruments. Once embedded in a
decision process they become part of a system's architecture, selecting for
some behaviours over others. This matters increasingly for AI, where
evaluation frameworks do not merely track capability but participate in
determining what capability comes to mean — and where model outputs are
beginning to be interpreted as measurements about people.
